questions.question: Explain the relationship between Information Literacy and critical thinking. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Information literacy is the ability to locate, evaluate, and use information effectively (U)/
  • (CO 1 ) Critical thinking involves analysing, evaluating, and interpreting information
  • logically. Critical thinking helps analyse, question, and judge the quality and credibility of
  • information It Shows that both skills support informed decision-making, problem-solving, and
  • academic research Information literacy provides access to information, while critical thinking
  • helps interpret and apply it responsibly.
  • Marking:

questions.question: Describe how libraries have evolved from ancient times to modern times. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:

  • Alexandria) (U)/ (CO1) Medieval Libraries: Restricted access; handwritten manuscripts; monastic
  • libraries. Renaissance & Printing Era: Printing press increased book availability and widened access.
  • Modern Public Libraries (19th –20th Century): Open access, lending services, classification, and
  • organization. Digital & Electronic Libraries (21st Century): Digital resources, e -services, online
  • catalogues, ICT, and smart library systems.

questions.question: Describe the purpose of an OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue) in libraries. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Meaning of OPAC and Definition: OPAC stands for Online Public Access Catalogue. (U)/CO1)
  • It is a digital catalogue used in libraries to help users search and locate the materials available in the
  • library.
  • OPAC is an online searchable database that provides information about all the books, journals, e-
  • resources, and other materials available in a library, along with their location and availability status.
  • Any 4-5 key purposes: Search features, real-time status, user services, digital links etc
  • 2–3 benefits: Time saving, transparency, efficiency
  • Conclusion: OPAC’s role in modern libraries: OPAC plays a vital role in modern libraries by making
  • information easy to find, improving user experience, and supporting efficient library management.
  • Marking:
  • a) Meaning, definition, purpose, benefits and conclusion is written Full mark (1+1+5+2+1)
  • b) Any Related Idea Half Mark
  • c) Any Attempt Three Mark
